title: Nurse-to-patient Ratio and Efforts to Reduce Nurses' Administrative Workload
what_it_is: Nurse-to-patient Ratio and Efforts to Reduce Nurses' Administrative Workload

sections.label: Nurse ratios and administrative workload
sections.summary: Questions ask for average and median nurse-to-patient ratios in general wards and ICUs, and steps to reduce nurses' administrative workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health for each year in the past five years, what is the average and median nurse-to-patient ratio for (i) general wards and (ii) intensive care units respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what steps has the Ministry taken to reduce the administrative workload of nurses in restructured hospitals; (b) whether additional steps will be taken; and (c) if so, what are they.

sections.label: Nurse attrition rates
sections.summary: Local public sector nurse attrition rose from 6% in 2017 to 7.4% in 2021, while foreign nurse attrition rose from 8.2% to 14.8%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The attrition of local public sector nurses increased from 6% in 2017, to 6.3% in 2018 and 7% in 2019, then dropped to 5.4% in 2020, before increasing to 7.4% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For foreign public sector nurses, international competition has been more intense and attrition rate has increased more significantly, from 8.2% in 2017, to 9.1% in 2018 and 9.4% in 2019, then dropped to 7% in 2020, before increasing to 14.8% in 2021.

sections.label: Nurse annual salaries
sections.summary: Median annual salaries for SNs rose from $42,800-$53,700 in 2017 to $46,300-$58,500 in 2021, and for SSNs from $65,000-$79,700 to $71,200-$87,600.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The median annual salaries for SNs ranged from $42,800 to $53,700 in 2017, and rose to $46,300 to $58,500 in 2021, while that for SSNs ranged from $65,000 to $79,700 in 2017, increasing to $71,200 to $87,600 in 2021.

sections.label: Nurse stock, intake and salaries
sections.summary: Registered nurse stock rose from around 42,800 at end 2019 to 43,000 at end 2021, local nursing intakes rose from around 1,500 in 2014 to around 2,100 in 2021, and local nurse salaries increased.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In fact, the registered stock of nurses over the past few years has remained stable, with a slight increase from around 42,800 at end 2019, to 43,000 at end 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Local nursing intakes have also increased from around 1,500 in 2014 to around 2,100 in 2021, to ensure that there is a stable inflow of nursing manpower into our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Over the last five years, the annual salaries of local nurses in public healthcare institutions – which comprises base salary, allowances and bonuses – have increased.

sections.label: Local nurse numbers stabilising
sections.summary: Local nurse numbers are stabilising, while the key problem is losing foreign nurses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The numbers that we are looking at in respect of the local nurses are actually stabilising.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Our key issue and problems are that we are losing the foreign nurses.

sections.label: Manpower loss and root causes
sections.summary: Local numbers are being lost, and while salaries and working conditions are constantly reviewed, they should not be assumed to always be the root of manpower problems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: That means that we are losing the numbers on the ground here, locally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, while salaries and working conditions are important and we are constantly looking at how we can improve these, we should not jump to the conclusion that they are always the root of the manpower problems.

sections.label: Staff Well-being Committee
sections.summary: An internal Staff Well-being Committee was set up, as mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Indeed, I understand the concerns and I mentioned earlier that there was an internal committee that was set up, the Staff Well-being Committee.

sections.label: Task force on abuse
sections.summary: A task force addresses abuse affecting staff and nurses' work conditions, and recommendations will be rolled out over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The culture may be different elsewhere, and we may want to educate and look into this matter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There is also a task force that is looking to address issues of abuse, which also impacts the work conditions of the staff and the nurses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: These are also all things that we are currently looking at.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, give us some time to roll out some of the recommendations that have been put up.
